executive_summary: JSW Steel combines record sales with a stronger balance sheet, but a larger capex program raises the importance of steel spreads and cash returns. September revenue and PAT grew strongly, while Q3 coking-coal inflation is an explicit counterweight to better volumes and pricing.
research_stance: Cyclical growth with improving financial capacity; judge on normalized EBITDA per tonne and full-cycle capital returns rather than reported P/E alone.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹54,486.00 crore, +20.7% YoY and +15.0% QoQ. PAT was ₹5,359.00 crore, +225.6% YoY and +14.1% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹10,120.00 crore and OPM 19.00%, compared with 16.00% a year earlier and 20.00% in June 2026. PAT margin was 9.84%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

The call reports adjusted EBITDA ₹9,941 crore at about 18% margin, whereas the local operating-profit line is ₹10,120 crore and rounded OPM 19%. These definitions must remain separate. Q4 FY26 local PAT ₹19,243 crore is an obvious outlier relative to surrounding quarters and makes the trailing earnings multiple unsuitable as a clean normalized valuation anchor; this report does not attribute that outlier to a specific transaction without a bridge.

FY26 annual CFO was ₹25,152 crore and free cash flow ₹10,610 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹69,820 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 11.00% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return.

thesis_drivers.title: Record volumes demonstrate asset execution
thesis_drivers.evidence: Consolidated Q2 sales reached 7.46 million tonnes, +13% YoY; Indian sales 7.27 million tonnes were +14%. BF3 at Vijayanagar reached about 90% utilization and Indian operations were about 88%, leaving room for throughput growth.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Value-added steel supports demand quality
thesis_drivers.evidence: Value-added/special product sales were 4.11 million tonnes and automotive volumes grew 36% YoY in the call. This improves customer mix, but does not remove commodity-price or imported-coal exposure.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Balance sheet can fund expansion, with a much larger commitment
thesis_drivers.evidence: Call net debt ₹44,482 crore and net debt/EBITDA 1.28x provide headroom. The expanded plan is ₹1.48 lakh crore over 5–6 years versus ₹1.3 lakh crore previously discussed; this creates a lasting capex and execution obligation.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Captive raw material is a delayed cost lever
thesis_drivers.evidence: The Odisha slurry pipeline targets March 2027 and Karnataka iron-ore additions Q4 FY27. Mozambique cleaned coking-coal production is expected from CY2028, so near-term coal inflation remains exposed.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

industry_context.heading: Steel demand and spreads
industry_context.content: Domestic demand supports capacity utilization, while realizations must offset coking coal and iron ore. Management expects Indian steel demand growth of 7–8% for FY27; this is its outlook, not an assured sales rate.

industry_context.heading: Expansion and JVs
industry_context.content: JV capacity adds scale but demands a separate debt/equity-accounting assessment. Management says JSW Steel is ring-fenced from the Sambalpur JV funding risk; legal and guarantee terms still determine the economic exposure.

business_economics: The operating bridge must start with separate production and sales volumes. Consolidated sales were 7.46mt, while crude production was 7.27mt; Indian sales happened also to be 7.27mt. Conflating these creates false utilization and realization calculations. BF3 at about 90% utilization demonstrates ramp progress, while group contribution depends on the wider product and geographic mix.

Management adjusted EBITDA divided by consolidated sales implies approximately ₹13,326 per sold tonne (₹9,941cr/7.46mt). This is analyst arithmetic on the disclosed group scope. An illustrative ₹1,000/tonne margin change at unchanged quarterly sales changes EBITDA by roughly ₹746cr—showing why steel spread normalization matters more than trailing P/E optics.
earnings_quality: Headline revenue and PAT match the local table, but adjusted EBITDA does not equal generic operating profit. Keep ₹9,941cr and ₹10,120cr as separate definitions until exceptional items, other income and consolidation adjustments are bridged. A 1% reconciliation rule would not permit these two figures to be labelled identical.

The JV discussion includes a stamp-duty provision and separate operating results. Current consolidated profit and historic EPS can therefore change with transaction and ownership accounting; a peak-quarter annualization cannot substitute for a consistent perimeter or mid-cycle earnings estimate.
capital_allocation: H1 spend represents approximately 46–51% of the FY27 capex envelope. Growth in operating cash flow must fund the remaining ₹10.9–12.9kcr annual spend as well as dividends, taxes and working capital; the multi-year ₹1.48 lakh crore programme creates further sequencing exposure.

Low current leverage creates flexibility rather than a guarantee. Stress the plan with a two-year margin downturn, delayed mine output and slower ramp-up. Management’s description of JV ring-fencing is valuable but should be checked against shareholder loans, guarantees and committed equity—not assumed from a single call answer.
valuation_logic: Use a sum of operating steel assets, JV interests and raw-material projects, with consistent consolidation and net debt. Do not value the same JV EBITDA inside consolidated earnings and again as a separate equity stake. Captive-mine benefits begin only after production, yield, logistics and operating costs are demonstrated.

A reverse enterprise-value case should show the normal sold-tonne base, sustainable EBITDA/tonne, capital expenditure and eventual distributable cash. The bull case needs volume gains to survive higher coal costs; the base case should allow moderate spreads and full project funding; the bear case should include both EBITDA contraction and higher debt.
peer_positioning: Tata Steel introduces different geographic and European restructuring exposures; Jindal Steel has a different ramp-up and ore-logistics profile; SAIL differs in project/employee economics. These are useful cycle checks, not interchangeable multiples. Compare EBITDA/tonne, cash conversion, net debt and maintenance/growth capex on matching operating scopes.
